note.headline: Apple at 358.54, near resistance, still above every value estimate; wait

summary.thesis: Apple is a strong, cash-rich business, but at 358.54 the price assumes much faster cash growth than Apple is showing, while analysts keep trimming forecasts.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait for a lower price. Swing: wait, because the price is sitting just under resistance.
summary.act_at: Long-term buy from 300.56, add at 273.62; swing only on a close above 361.86

note.happening: Apple closed at 358.54, up 0.83% on the day. It is still in an uptrend and sits just below a resistance zone of 359.8–361.86. Today's news is only Black Friday deal roundups on Apple gear (reported by The Verge). The next earnings report is due on 2027-01-28.
note.business: The headlines are about sentiment, not the business. Discounts on AirPods, MacBooks and Apple Watch are seasonal retail news and do not change Apple's demand or margins by themselves. The numbers that do matter are mixed. On the good side, trailing revenue grew 15.06% to 478.8B, free cash flow (cash left after running and investing in the business) rose to 136.1B from 98.8B, and the operating margin improved to 33.01% from 31.97%. On the weaker side, quarterly sales growth slowed to 11.72% from 16.6% two quarters ago. Inventory is up 154% against sales up 12%, which can force price cuts if the product does not sell. Analysts have cut next-quarter EPS (earnings per share) by 3.8% over 30 days. The annual report also adds a new investigation risk; that is a governance issue for now, not a demand issue. Apple has more debt than cash (net cash is -23.4B), but liquidity of 56.7B against cash flow of 136.1B means its cash position is not at risk. What is at risk is margins, if the inventory build has to be cleared at a discount.

worth.text: Every method puts fair value below today's price. A discounted cash flow model (today's value of future cash) gives 145.37 in the bear case, 202.38 in the base case and 265.87 in the bull case, using a 9.9% discount rate. Apple's own 5-year price-to-sales history gives 222.1 to 300.56. The stock trades at 39.9 times trailing earnings and 33.8 times next year's earnings. Its price-to-sales of 10.9 compares with a peer median of 5.3 and is at the 100th percentile of its own 5-year range. The gap between the models and the price comes down to one assumption, the starting growth rate of free cash flow. The price implies 27.1% a year. At 20% the value is 273.62, and only at 30% does the value reach 400.49. Last year's sales growth was 15%. Margins matter too: if the operating margin fell to 24%, the value would drop to 204.81.
worth.key_assumption: The price needs free cash flow to start growing at about 27.1% a year, well above last year's 15% sales growth.

bull: Free cash flow rose to 136.1B from 98.8B over the trailing year, which leaves a lot of cash for buybacks.
The operating margin improved to 33.01% from 31.97%, so Apple is keeping more of each sale.
The share count fell 1.56% in a year, and the price is above its rising 50-day average of 343.27, which keeps the trend up.
bear: Inventory is up 154% while quarterly sales are up 12%. Unsold product can force price cuts that would hurt margins.

Price-to-sales of 10.9 is about double the peer median of 5.3, while quarterly growth slowed to 11.72% from 16.6%.

levels.what: Today's close. It is above the whole value range of 145.37–300.56, so it is too high to buy.
The top of the value range and of Apple's own price-to-sales history, near the 200-day average of 304.38. Buying starts here.

longterm.why: The business is good, but the price assumes growth Apple is not showing, and forecasts are being cut. The rule verdict is 'Too expensive' and the committee call is Hold.

swing.why: The price is less than one typical daily move (the average true range, or ATR, is 8.23) below resistance at 359.8–361.86, and the macro read is negative. No trade until a close above 361.86, or a pullback that holds support at 347.89–351.46.

decision.timing: Options price a 5.1% move by 2026-12-18 and a 10.4% move by 2027-02-19, a window that covers the 2027-01-28 report. There is no long-term buy above 300.56 before that report shows whether the inventory build hurt margins.

change_mind: The price falls to 300.56 or below, the top of the value range, while the business numbers stay the same. That turns 'wait' into 'buy'.
The 2027-01-28 report shows the operating margin at or above 33.01% and inventory no longer growing far faster than sales. That would weaken the margin-risk bear case.
Next-year EPS estimates climb back above the 10.84 they stood at 30 days ago, which would reverse the current downward revisions.
note.what_changed: Unchanged: still wait, because the close of 358.54 remains above the top of the value range at 300.56, and the growth the price implies edged up to 27.1% from 26.8%.
